clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old healthy anesthetist with 5 weeks of occupational exposure to COVID-19 patients presented with sudden temporal relative scotoma in the left eye. Standard clinical examination including best-corrected visual acuity (20/20), pupillary assessment, color vision, visual field testing (SITA Fast 30-2), anterior segment examination, and standard fundoscopy were all unremarkable. Fluorescein angiography showed no leakage or vascular exudation. However, swept-source OCT (SS-OCT) revealed a characteristic hyperreflective band at the level of the ganglion cell and inner plexiform layers, sparing the outer retina—a finding consistent with COVID-19-associated retinal microvascular involvement. At 30-day follow-up, the patient continued to report the scotoma, and retinal imaging demonstrated the same hyperreflective lesions with even greater intensity, with no arteries or veins in the inner retinal layers that could account for the hyperreflective shadow. Routine blood tests were normal with no coagulopathy alterations and normal blood pressure. RT-PCR testing was negative. The diagnosis of COVID-19 was established through the distinctive retinal imaging findings rather than through standard systemic testing or documented acute infection confirmation.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Sudden temporal relative scotoma in left eye as presenting symptom
Best-corrected visual acuity preserved at 20/20 despite scotoma
Standard fundoscopic examination unremarkable
Fluorescein angiography showed no leakage or vascular exudation
SS-OCT revealed hyperreflective band at ganglion cell and inner plexiform layers, sparing outer retina
Routine blood tests normal with no coagulopathy alterations
At 30-day follow-up, scotoma persisted with retinal imaging showing same hyperreflective lesions with greater intensity
No arteries or veins in inner retinal layers on B-scan causing hyperreflective shadow
RT-PCR testing was negative
5-week occupational exposure to COVID-19 patients prior to symptom onset

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Acute retinal necrosis or other infectious retinitis
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Unremarkable standard fundoscopy, no leakage on FA, preserved visual acuity, and characteristic inner retinal hyperreflectivity pattern on OCT rather than outer retinal involvement
No arteries or veins in inner retinal layers on B-scan causing hyperreflective shadow; unremarkable FA
Normal blood tests with no coagulopathy alterations; normal blood pressure

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Acute COVID-19 with active viral replication
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: RT-PCR was negative; presentation appears to be post-exposure with retinal manifestation rather than acute systemic infection

remaining_uncertainties: Serological confirmation of COVID-19 infection (anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies) not documented in available source evidence
Presence or absence of systemic COVID-19 symptoms during exposure period or at symptom onset not documented
Exact temporal relationship between COVID-19 infection and retinal symptom onset not established
Treatment provided and clinical response not documented
Final clinical outcome and resolution status of scotoma not documented
Mechanism of COVID-19-associated inner retinal hyperreflectivity (microvascular inflammation, endothelial involvement, or other pathophysiology) not explicitly detailed
